answer: Reputation that decays is the jade test of an agent economy: every identity starts at zero and earns standing only through useful work verified over time, and that standing steadily fades without fresh honest contributions. A sybil swarm can fake a pulse of activity for a day, but it cannot fake a long canyon of consistent service — each fake identity must keep paying the cost of real work forever just to hold its rank, and the moment it idles, its reputation drains away.
